questions.q: A 35-year-old man presents with a painless, indurated, clean-based ulcer on the glans penis for 2 weeks. Inguinal lymph nodes are enlarged but non-tender. Dark-field microscopy of the lesion exudate shows motile spirochetes. What is the most appropriate first-line treatment?
opts: Benzathine penicillin G 2.4 million units IM single dose
Doxycycline 100 mg twice daily for 14 days
questions.exp: Primary syphilis (chancre) is caused by Treponema pallidum. Benzathine penicillin G 2.4 MU IM single dose is the first-line treatment. Doxycycline is an alternative for penicillin-allergic patients.

questions.q: A 28-year-old woman with a history of butterfly facial rash, photosensitivity, and oral ulcers presents with a 4+ proteinuria. Antinuclear antibody (ANA) is positive with anti-dsDNA elevated. Which skin finding is most specific for this diagnosis?
questions.exp: Systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) classically presents with a malar (butterfly) rash that characteristically spares the nasolabial folds. Gottron's papules and heliotrope rash are features of dermatomyositis.

questions.q: A 45-year-old farmer presents with a slowly enlarging, painless, indurated plaque on the dorsum of the right hand. The plaque has been present for 6 months and shows central scarring with satellite nodules. Lymphangitic streaks are absent. KOH mount shows thick-walled muriform cells. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.exp: Chromoblastomycosis presents with verrucous plaques that show central scarring and satellite nodules. The diagnostic hallmark on histology/KOH is muriform (sclerotic/Medlar) cells — thick-walled, brown, septate cells.

questions.q: A 22-year-old man presents with multiple grouped vesicles on an erythematous base on the shaft of the penis, accompanied by burning and inguinal lymphadenopathy. He reports a similar episode 3 months ago. Tzanck smear shows multinucleated giant cells. What is the most appropriate long-term management to prevent recurrences?
opts: Oral valacyclovir 500 mg daily suppressive therapy
Oral acyclovir 400 mg three times daily for 5 days episodically
questions.exp: Recurrent genital herpes (HSV-2 typically) with frequent episodes is best managed with daily suppressive therapy. Valacyclovir 500 mg OD reduces recurrence frequency and transmission risk. Episodic therapy is less effective than suppressive for frequent recurrences (>6/year).

questions.q: A 30-year-old leprosy patient on multidrug therapy (MDT) develops sudden painless loss of vision in one eye, along with uveitis and a new tender erythematous nodular eruption on his legs over 3 days. The skin lesions are warm and tender. This reaction is best classified as:
questions.exp: Erythema nodosum leprosum (ENL / Type 2 reaction) occurs in lepromatous and borderline lepromatous leprosy. It presents with tender nodules, systemic features, uveitis, and orchitis. It is immune complex-mediated (Type III hypersensitivity). Treatment is thalidomide or corticosteroids.

questions.q: A 60-year-old man presents with a tense blistering eruption involving flexures, trunk, and limbs without mucosal involvement. Direct immunofluorescence (DIF) shows linear IgG and C3 along the basement membrane zone. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.exp: Bullous pemphigoid presents with tense blisters, typically in the elderly, without significant mucosal involvement. DIF shows linear IgG and C3 at the BMZ (sub-epidermal level). Pemphigus shows intraepidermal blister with IgG on keratinocyte surfaces (fish-net pattern).

questions.q: A 25-year-old woman with recurrent painful oral ulcers since 2 years presents with new genital ulcers and hypopyon (pus in the anterior chamber of the eye). Pathergy test is positive. Which HLA type is most strongly associated with this condition?
questions.exp: Behcet's disease presents with the triad of oral ulcers, genital ulcers, and uveitis (often with hypopyon). A positive pathergy test is characteristic. It is strongly associated with HLA-B51, especially in Middle Eastern and Asian populations.

questions.q: A 40-year-old woman with psoriasis presents with silvery scaling plaques on the extensor surfaces. She is started on methotrexate. Which baseline investigation is most critical to monitor before initiating therapy?
opts: Liver function tests and complete blood count
questions.exp: Methotrexate is hepatotoxic and myelosuppressive. Baseline LFTs, CBC, renal function, and a chest X-ray are essential. LFT and CBC are most critical as hepatotoxicity and bone marrow suppression are the major adverse effects requiring monitoring.

questions.q: A 5-year-old child presents with honey-colored crusted lesions around the nose and mouth after a recent upper respiratory infection. Culture grows gram-positive cocci in clusters. The most appropriate treatment is:
questions.exp: Impetigo is usually caused by Staphylococcus aureus (or Streptococcus pyogenes). Localized impetigo is best treated with topical mupirocin 2% or retapamulin. Oral antibiotics (dicloxacillin, cephalexin) are used for widespread disease. Penicillin is ineffective against S. aureus.

questions.q: A 33-year-old HIV-positive patient with a CD4 count of 60 cells/μL develops painful grouped vesicles along a single dermatome on the trunk. He also has hyperalgesia and allodynia in the same area. The most important complication to prevent is:
questions.exp: Herpes zoster in an immunocompromised patient (like HIV) carries risk of dissemination and post-herpetic neuralgia (PHN). PHN — pain persisting >3 months after rash — is the most common complication and must be prevented with early antiviral therapy (acyclovir/valacyclovir within 72 hours of rash onset).

questions.q: A 50-year-old man presents with an enlarging pearly nodule with rolled edges, telangiectasias, and central ulceration on his nose. He is a retired outdoor worker with extensive sun exposure history. Biopsy shows nests of basaloid cells with peripheral palisading. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.exp: Basal cell carcinoma (BCC) is the most common skin cancer. The nodular type presents with a pearly papule/nodule with rolled borders, telangiectasias, and central ulceration on sun-exposed areas. Histology shows basaloid cells with peripheral palisading and stromal retraction artifact.

questions.q: A 19-year-old presents with multiple comedones, papules, and pustules on the face and upper chest. She is prescribed oral isotretinoin. Which of the following is an absolute contraindication to this drug?
questions.exp: Isotretinoin is a potent teratogen (Pregnancy Category X). It causes severe fetal malformations (craniofacial, cardiac, CNS defects). It is absolutely contraindicated in pregnancy. iPLEDGE program mandates 2 forms of contraception for females of childbearing potential.

questions.q: A leprosy patient classified as borderline tuberculoid (BT) has a single large hypopigmented anaesthetic patch on the thigh with a thickened superficial peroneal nerve. What is the WHO-recommended MDT regimen?
opts: Multibacillary MDT for 12 months (rifampicin + dapsone + clofazimine)
questions.exp: BT leprosy (1–5 skin lesions) is classified as paucibacillary (PB). WHO PB MDT: rifampicin 600 mg once monthly + dapsone 100 mg daily for 6 months. MB MDT (triple therapy for 12 months) is for multibacillary disease (>5 lesions or positive smear).

questions.q: A 28-year-old pregnant woman at 32 weeks presents with intensely pruritic urticarial papules and plaques starting on the abdomen, spreading to extremities, but sparing the umbilicus. Biopsy shows perivascular eosinophils and spongiosis. Direct IF is negative. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.exp: Polymorphic eruption of pregnancy (PEP/PUPPP) typically starts in the striae of the abdomen in late pregnancy, characteristically sparing the umbilicus. It is the most common dermatosis of pregnancy. DIF is negative, distinguishing it from pemphigoid gestationis (DIF: C3 linear at BMZ).

questions.q: A 17-year-old presents with intensely pruritic, grouped, symmetrically distributed papules and vesicles on the elbows, knees, and buttocks. Biopsy shows neutrophil microabscesses at dermal papillae tips. DIF shows granular IgA deposits at the dermal papillae. What is the associated systemic condition?
questions.exp: Dermatitis herpetiformis (DH) is characterized by granular IgA deposits at the dermal papillae on DIF. It is strongly associated with celiac disease (gluten-sensitive enteropathy). Treatment includes dapsone (for itch) and a strict gluten-free diet (treats both skin and gut disease).

questions.q: A 45-year-old man with HIV presents with multiple rapidly growing, painful red-purple nodular lesions on the skin, oral mucosa, and gastrointestinal tract. His CD4 count is 45 cells/μL. The causative agent is:
questions.exp: Kaposi's sarcoma (KS) in AIDS is caused by HHV-8 (Kaposi's sarcoma-associated herpesvirus, KSHV). It presents with violaceous/red-purple skin plaques and nodules, oral mucosa involvement, and can affect visceral organs. Treatment involves antiretroviral therapy and chemotherapy (liposomal doxorubicin).

questions.q: A 55-year-old woman presents with Raynaud's phenomenon, puffy fingers, skin tightening of hands and face, and dysphagia. ANA is positive with anti-Scl-70 (anti-topoisomerase I) antibody. What is the most likely prognosis-determining complication?
questions.exp: Diffuse cutaneous systemic sclerosis (with anti-Scl-70) is associated with a high risk of interstitial lung disease (ILD), which is the leading cause of death in these patients. Anti-centromere antibody is associated with limited cutaneous SSc and pulmonary arterial hypertension.

questions.q: During a Mohs micrographic surgery, which frozen section technique allows examination of 100% of the surgical margin?
opts: Excision with 4mm margins and paraffin sections
questions.exp: Mohs micrographic surgery uses horizontal (en face) frozen sections of the excised tissue, allowing 100% of the peripheral and deep margins to be examined microscopically. Standard breadloaf (vertical) sections only examine approximately 1% of the total margin.

questions.q: A 30-year-old woman presents with butterfly-shaped erythema on her cheeks and nasal bridge, a maculopapular rash on sun-exposed areas, and periungual telangiectasias. She has proximal muscle weakness and elevated CK levels. Anti-Jo-1 antibodies are positive. The most likely associated systemic complication is:
questions.exp: Anti-Jo-1 (anti-synthetase) antibodies in dermatomyositis/polymyositis are strongly associated with antisynthetase syndrome, which includes interstitial lung disease, mechanic's hands, Raynaud phenomenon, and myositis. ILD is the main morbidity and mortality determinant.

questions.q: A 25-year-old man from Bihar presents with an indurated painless papule on the cheek that slowly enlarged to a nodule, then ulcerated. He had traveled to a rural endemic area 3 months ago. Slit-skin smear from the edge of the lesion shows intracellular amastigotes in macrophages. The most likely causative species for this localized cutaneous disease in India is:
questions.exp: Cutaneous leishmaniasis in India (Oriental sore) is primarily caused by Leishmania tropica (dry/urban form) and L. major (wet/rural form). L. donovani causes visceral leishmaniasis (kala-azar) in India. L. braziliensis causes mucocutaneous leishmaniasis in South America.

questions.q: A 12-year-old boy presents with scaling of the scalp with fluorescence under Wood's lamp (blue-green). Culture on Sabouraud's dextrose agar shows a greenish colony. The causative organism most likely causing endothrix infection is:
questions.exp: Trichophyton violaceum (and T. tonsurans) cause endothrix tinea capitis — hyphae and spores are within the hair shaft (no fluorescence). However, T. schoenleinii causes favus with dull-green fluorescence. Microsporum species fluoresce bright blue-green and cause ectothrix infection. The question intends T. violaceum for endothrix (non-fluorescing) — among the options, T. violaceum is the endothrix type.

questions.q: A 38-year-old man presents with chronic scaling and hyperpigmented plaques on his elbows, knees, scalp, and lumbar area for 5 years. Auspitz sign is positive. He also has pitting of fingernails. Which cytokine pathway is the primary therapeutic target in severe plaque psoriasis?
questions.exp: Psoriasis is driven primarily by the IL-23/Th17 axis. Biologics targeting IL-17A (secukinumab, ixekizumab), IL-17RA (brodalumab), and IL-23 (guselkumab, risankizumab, tildrakizumab) are highly effective. TNF-α inhibitors are also used but IL-17/IL-23 agents show superior efficacy. IL-4/IL-13 targeting (dupilumab) is for atopic dermatitis.

questions.q: A 6-month-old infant presents with intensely pruritic erythematous vesicular and weeping patches on both cheeks and scalp, sparing the diaper area. There is a family history of asthma. Total IgE is elevated. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.exp: Infantile atopic dermatitis (eczema) presents in the first 6 months with pruritic eczematous lesions on the face (cheeks, forehead) and scalp, with sparing of the diaper area. Family history of atopy and elevated IgE are characteristic. Seborrheic dermatitis presents with greasy, non-pruritic scaling.

questions.q: A 44-year-old woman presents with recurrent chronic urticaria for 6 months (>6 weeks) unresponsive to antihistamines. Autologous serum skin test is positive. Which of the following is the most appropriate next-line treatment?
questions.exp: Chronic spontaneous urticaria (CSU) refractory to antihistamines is treated with omalizumab (anti-IgE), which is FDA-approved for this indication and is the second-line standard of care per international guidelines (EAACI/GA²LEN/EDF/WAO). Cyclosporine is third-line. Systemic steroids are only for short-term use.

questions.q: A 23-year-old sexually active man presents with a painless, firm, rubbery inguinal lymph node enlargement on one side, without associated genital ulcer. He reports a self-healing genital papule 3 weeks earlier. Complement fixation titer for Chlamydia trachomatis is elevated. The most likely diagnosis is:
questions.exp: Lymphogranuloma venereum (LGV) is caused by C. trachomatis serovars L1, L2, L3. The primary lesion is a transient painless papule/ulcer. The secondary stage shows painful (classically described as) suppurative inguinal lymphadenopathy (buboes). Complement fixation titer >1:64 is diagnostic. Treatment is doxycycline 100 mg BD × 21 days.

questions.q: A 29-year-old woman presents with peri-orbital oedema, heliotrope discoloration of the eyelids, and Gottron's papules over the MCP and PIP joints of both hands. Proximal muscle weakness is present. Which malignancy should be most actively screened for in this adult patient?
questions.exp: Dermatomyositis in adults has a 15–30% association with internal malignancy. In women, ovarian cancer is most commonly associated. Other associations include lung, breast, GI, and nasopharyngeal cancers. Comprehensive cancer screening (CT chest/abdomen/pelvis, pelvic ultrasound, CA-125) is mandatory in adult-onset dermatomyositis.

questions.q: A 70-year-old man presents with a rapidly growing, firm, painless papule on the lower lip that has enlarged to 1.5 cm in 2 months. Biopsy shows atypical keratinocytes invading the dermis with keratin pearls and individual cell dyskeratosis. Regional lymph nodes are not palpable. What is the most important prognostic risk factor for metastasis in this lesion?
opts: Tumor depth (thickness) > 2 mm and perineural invasion
questions.exp: Squamous cell carcinoma (SCC) high-risk features for metastasis include tumor thickness >2 mm, Clark level ≥ IV, perineural invasion, poor differentiation, location on the ear/lip, and immunosuppression. Perineural invasion is a key independent prognostic factor for recurrence and metastasis.

questions.q: Which of the following correctly describes the mechanism of action of dapsone in leprosy?
opts: Inhibits protein synthesis at the 50S ribosomal subunit
questions.exp: Dapsone (a sulfone) is a competitive antagonist of para-aminobenzoic acid (PABA) and inhibits dihydropteroate synthase, blocking folate synthesis in Mycobacterium leprae (similar to sulfonamides). Rifampicin inhibits RNA polymerase; clofazimine disrupts DNA template function and membrane integrity.

questions.q: A 35-year-old man presents with depigmented macules on the dorsum of both hands and feet, along with loss of sensation in these areas. Slit-skin smear is negative. Nerve biopsy shows granulomatous inflammation around and within the nerve fascicles (perineural and intraneural). What is the Ridley-Jopling classification?
questions.exp: Tuberculoid leprosy (TT) shows well-defined granulomas with CD4+ T-cells, Langerhans-type giant cells, and perineural/intraneural inflammation on nerve biopsy. There are few (1–2) well-defined anaesthetic hypopigmented patches. Slit-skin smear is negative. High cell-mediated immunity.

questions.q: A patient undergoes a 4 mm punch biopsy of a pigmented lesion on the arm. The biopsy confirms melanoma with Breslow thickness 1.2 mm, no ulceration, and mitotic rate <1/mm². According to AJCC staging, what is the most appropriate surgical management?
opts: Wide local excision with 1 cm margin
Wide local excision with 1–2 cm margin and sentinel lymph node biopsy
Wide local excision with 2 cm margin only
Wide local excision with 2 cm margin and elective lymph node dissection
questions.exp: For melanoma 1.01–2.0 mm Breslow thickness (T2), current guidelines recommend wide local excision with 1–2 cm margins and sentinel lymph node biopsy (SLNB) to assess nodal status. SLNB is recommended for T1b (>0.8 mm or ulcerated) through T4 lesions. Elective lymph node dissection is no longer standard.

questions.q: A 32-year-old woman with type IV skin (Fitzpatrick) wishes to undergo laser hair removal. Which laser is most appropriate for her skin type to minimize the risk of post-inflammatory hyperpigmentation?
questions.exp: Nd:YAG 1064 nm laser has the deepest penetration and least melanin absorption among hair removal lasers. It is the safest for darker skin types (Fitzpatrick IV–VI) as it bypasses epidermal melanin most effectively, reducing the risk of post-inflammatory hyperpigmentation and burns. Alexandrite and Ruby are safer for skin types I–III.
